# @cubicecho/agent-core

> The endpoint-agnostic half of an OpenAI-compatible agent loop: tool-schema compatibility, on-demand tool loading, one-shot side tasks, run events, and a pooled client.

What is here is everything that does not know what the agent is *for*: making a tool schema a strict server will accept, getting tool definitions in front of a model without paying for all of them, reading one streamed turn back into a message, answering an endpoint that refuses one of those, one-shot calls that support a run, the host's side of lifecycle hooks, the event bus a watcher reads, a pooled client, and the rules about retrying. What is not here is the work — orchestration, prompts, and whatever the run is about — because that is the caller's, and it is the part that differs between one server and the next.

Requires Node >=22, with `openai` >=6 as a peer dependency. ESM only.
Full prose, worked examples and the reasoning behind each seam are in README.md; this file is the index.

## Exports

### agent-loop

The loop above a turn: send, run the tools the model asked for, send again, until it stops asking.

- `AgentLoopHooks` (type) — The hooks a loop runs around one question.
- `AgentLoopOptions` (type) — What `runAgentLoop` takes.
- `AgentLoopResult` (type) — What a finished loop hands back.
- `buildBody` — The one place a streamed request's body is decided from a config and what the endpoint and the model have refused.
- `preselect` — The tools a request is likely to need, picked by a small model before the run starts, or none.
- `preview` — A long tool argument or result cut to what a watcher needs, with the full length said.
- `resolveApiKey` — The key to send, where an endpoint may inherit one from the settings it overrides.
- `runAgentLoop` — Runs a question to its answer: one `runTurn` per step, the tools it asks for between them, until a turn asks for none.
- `ToolCallOutcome` (type) — What one tool call did, in the order the model asked.
- `ToolCallRequest` (type) — One call the model made, as `dispatch` is handed it.

### calibration

How many characters a token is worth on one model, learned from what its endpoint reports.

- `calibrate` — Takes one reading from a request that was answered, so the next one to this model is sized by it.
- `charsPerTokenFor` — The characters per token to size a request to this model with, `CHARS_PER_TOKEN` until a turn has reported one.
- `resetCalibration` — Forgets every reading, so the next request is sized at `CHARS_PER_TOKEN` again.

### capabilities

What an endpoint turned out not to support, and answering it when it says so.

- `Capabilities` (type) — What one endpoint turned out not to support.
- `capabilitiesFor` — What this endpoint is known not to support.
- `ModelCapabilities` (type) — What one model on that endpoint turned out not to support.
- `modelCapabilitiesFor` — What this model on this endpoint is known not to support.
- `NegotiateOptions` (type) — What `negotiate` takes besides the request.
- `negotiate` — Sends a request, re-sending it each time the answer is this endpoint refusing something the request can do without.
- `resetCapabilities` — Forgets every endpoint's capabilities.

### catalog

The contract between whatever holds the tools and the loop that offers them to a model.

- `CatalogServer` (type) — One server's tools, without their JSON schemas — the cheap half of a tool definition.

### client

- `ClientPoolOptions` (type) — What the client pool is held to across a process.
- `configureClients` — Changes what the client pool is held to, for a process whose endpoints are not shaped like the deployments these defaults were chosen for.
- `contextLimitFor` — How much a model will read, in tokens.
- `endpointId` — `endpointKey` hashed, for the remembered facts that can leave the process.
- `endpointKey` — What counts as one endpoint, everywhere in this package that has to remember something about one — the model listings, `capabilities`, and the no-thinking hints in `side-task`.
- `FIRST_TOKEN_FACTOR` — How many idle windows the first chunk gets when `firstTokenSeconds` is not given.
- `firstTokenMs` — The wait for a streamed turn's first chunk, in the SDK's spelling: `undefined` is no limit.
- `getClient` — The client for an endpoint, built once and kept.
- `listModels` — Asks an endpoint what it serves, and remembers the answer.
- `ModelInfo` (type) — A model an endpoint offers, and what it says the model will read.
- `NO_KEY` — The SDK insists on a non-empty key even where the server will not look at it.
- `resetClients` — Forgets every cached client and listing, and puts `configureClients` back to the defaults.
- `servedWindow` — The window a local server is actually serving a model in, which its listing does not say.
- `timeoutMs` — Zero, less, or absent means no limit, which the SDK spells as `undefined`.

### compaction

Keeping a long run inside its window: stale tool results cleared, and the oldest stretch folded into a summary the model writes itself.

- `COMPACT_AT` — The fraction of the window in use before a summary is worth its own round trip.
- `CompactionOptions` (type) — What `planCompaction` takes.
- `CompactionPlan` (type) — Where to cut, as `compactTranscript` takes it.
- `compactTranscript` — The transcript with the plan's stretch replaced by one system message holding its summary.
- `KEEP_RATIO` — The fraction of the window the kept tail may fill, leaving room for the run to grow again.
- `PruneOptions` (type) — What `pruneToolResults` takes.
- `planCompaction` — Where to fold a transcript that has grown into its window, or `undefined` when it should not be.
- `pruneToolResults` — The transcript with every tool result but the latest few replaced by a one-line stub.
- `SUMMARY_LEAD` — How a summary message opens, which is also how `planCompaction` knows one from a system prompt.
- `SUMMARY_PROMPT` — The summariser's instruction when the caller gives none.
- `summariser` — A summariser that asks `model` with `SUMMARY_PROMPT`, for `compactTranscript`.
- `summaryInput` — What the summariser is handed for a plan: the earlier summary if there was one, then each message as its role and at most 4000 characters of its text.

### config

What this package needs to know about a caller's configuration.

- `AgentConfig` (type) — A whole agent configuration — every part, plus the two fields that belong to no group.
- `Endpoint` (type) — Where to send a request and how long to wait.
- `ModelParams` (type) — What to ask the model for.
- `RetryPolicy` (type) — How many times a lost or refused request is worth sending again.
- `ToolPolicy` (type) — How tools reach the model, and how long it may keep calling them.

### continuation

Picking up an answer the token ceiling cut off, instead of keeping half of it.

- `ContinueTurnOptions` (type) — What `continueTurn` takes besides what `runTurn` does.
- `continueTurn` — Carries on an answer the token ceiling cut off, by sending the transcript again with the answer so far as a trailing assistant message, and joins the pieces into one turn.
- `isContinuable` — Whether a turn is one a continuation can finish: cut off at the ceiling, with an answer begun and no tool call in it.

### errors

- `errorMessage` — What went wrong, as a string.

### events

What a run is doing, while it is doing it.

- `configureEvents` — Changes what the bus keeps, for a process whose runs are not shaped like the ones these defaults were chosen for.
- `EventBusOptions` (type) — What the bus keeps and for how long.
- `emit` — Records one event and hands it to everyone watching that run.
- `endRun` — Forgets a run that will not be emitting `done` — one whose process is tearing down, or whose loop threw where it could not be caught.
- `fold` — Consecutive tokens of one kind are one thing being said, not hundreds of things.
- `history` — The backlog alone, for a caller that wants a snapshot rather than a subscription.
- `RunEvent` (type) — One thing that happened in a run, as a watcher receives it.
- `RunEventInput` (type) — What `emit` is given: the run and the sequence are the bus's to assign.
- `RunEventKind` (type) — Which kind of thing happened, and what `text`, `name`, `ok` and `usage` carry for it.
- `RunMetrics` (type) — A run summed and derived from its events: what it cost, where the time went, and why.
- `RunMetricsOptions` (type) — What `runMetrics` takes besides the events.
- `RunUsage` (type) — What a run has spent, counted from the start of the run rather than for the turn that carried it: a client draws the latest one it has seen and needs no arithmetic of its own, and one lost to the backlog cap costs nothing because the next supersedes it.
- `resetEvents` — Test seam: forget every run, so one test's events cannot be read by the next.
- `runMetrics` — A run's totals, timings and cache findings, derived from the events it emitted.
- `TurnReport` (type) — One turn's usage and measurements as a `usage` event carries them.
- `watch` — Everything that has happened on a run, then everything that happens next, until it ends.

### hooks

Lifecycle hooks, from the host's side: what a session looks like to them, where their context lands in a request, and what is said about each one.

- `assembleContext` — Builds the context a set of outcomes adds and the notes that go with it.
- `configureHooks` — Changes what hooks are held to, for a process whose windows are not the size these defaults were chosen for, or whose host wants its own name above the context.
- `consult` — Runs an event's hooks and waits for their say, for a host that will hold off when one of them vetoes.
- `Gathered` (type) — The context a set of outcomes adds to a request, and a note for each hook worth mentioning.
- `gather` — Runs the hooks ahead of a request and builds what they add to it.
- `HOOK_CONTEXT_TOKENS` — The most context all of a request's hooks add between them by default, in estimated tokens.
- `HOOK_EVENTS` — Every event a hook can be bound to, in the order a session meets them.
- `HOOK_PREFACE` — Said once, above the blocks, so the model reads them as background rather than instructions.
- `HookContext` (type) — What a host knows at an event.
- `HookEvent` (type) — A point in a session a hook can be bound to.
- `HookMessage` (type) — One message of a session as a hook is handed it.
- `HookNote` (type) — One hook's line for whoever is watching: the context it added, or why it added none.
- `HookOptions` (type) — What hooks are held to across a process.
- `HookOutcome` (type) — What one hook did.
- `HookRunner` (type) — Runs one event's hooks.
- `INJECT_EVENTS` — The events whose hooks run before a request, and so the only ones whose output can reach it.
- `notify` — Runs the hooks for an event that reads what happened and adds nothing to a request.
- `resetHooks` — Test seam: puts `configureHooks` back to the defaults, so one test's budget or preface is not the next's.
- `turnIndex` — Which turn of a session begins at a point, from 0: the user messages ahead of it.
- `turnMessages` — A stretch of a transcript as a hook reads it: what the user and the assistant said, and nothing else.
- `UNTRUSTED_PREFACE` — One sentence for a system prompt, saying what an `untrusted` block is.
- `untrusted` — Fences text nobody trusted — a fetched page, an email, a submitted card, a tool result — so the model can see where it starts and ends and read it as data rather than as instructions.
- `withContext` — The request, with the hooks' context added to this turn's question.

### reset

- `resetAll` — Forgets everything this package remembers between calls.

### retry

Everything about a request failing that is not about what the request said.

- `backoffMs` — Exponential, with jitter so several tasks failing at once do not return in lockstep.
- `CHARS_PER_TOKEN` — The divisor behind `estimateTokens`, applied here to a character count rather than a string.
- `ContextBreakdown` (type) — What a request is made of, by the part of it a consumer can actually do something about.
- `ContextBreakdownOptions` (type) — What `contextTokens` takes besides the request.
- `ContextOverflow` — The request was bigger than the model will read.
- `compact` — 1234 → "1.2k".
- `contextChars` — What each part of a request is worth in characters, by the same walk `requestTokens` divides.
- `contextTokens` — What each part of a request costs the window, in tokens, adding up to the whole.
- `EndpointSilent` — The endpoint stopped answering mid-request.
- `isModelLoading` — Whether a failure is a local server still loading the model, rather than one failing to serve.
- `isOverflow` — Whether a refusal means the request was too big, rather than merely refused.
- `isTransient` — Whether a failed request is worth trying again.
- `LOADING_POLL_MS` — How long to wait between asking a loading server again.
- `LOADING_TIMEOUT_MS` — How long `runTurn` waits for a model to load unless told otherwise.
- `messageTokens` — One message's estimated tokens, by the same count `requestTokens` sums for a whole request.
- `requestChars` — How many characters a request is worth: the walk `requestTokens` divides, without the division.
- `requestTokens` — What this request will cost the window, in tokens, near enough.
- `SMALLEST_LIKELY_WINDOW` — The smallest window worth believing in, and the floor under `runTurn`'s guard.
- `sleep` — A delay an abort cuts short, rejecting rather than resolving early.
- `TokenEstimateOptions` (type) — What the two token estimates below take besides what they measure.
- `toolsChars` — How many characters a tool array is worth, measured once per array.

### run-turn

One turn, given as many attempts as the caller allows.

- `RunTurnOptions` (type) — A retry is not the same event as a downgrade, but a watcher wants to be told about both.
- `runTurn` — `request` is a callback rather than a body because the body has to be rebuilt from whatever the last attempt latched off: the tools it sends depend on `strictSchemas`, and `relaxTools` has to apply to the schemas that were just sanitised.

### schema-compat

JSON Schema compatibility for llama.cpp-backed servers.

- `isGrammarError` — Does this failure look like the server could not build a grammar from our tool schemas?
- `relaxTools` — The retry shape: llama.cpp's converter rejects regex escape classes (`\d`, `\w`, `\s`) in `pattern` and most `format` values, both of which only ever narrowed a string the tool re-validates anyway.
- `sanitizeTools` — Tool definitions a strict server will accept, remembered per definition object.

### side-task

One-shot calls that support a run without being one: picking tools, naming a session, summarising a transcript, proposing follow-ups.

- `AskJsonOptions` (type) — What `askJson` takes besides a side task's options.
- `ask` — Runs a side task and returns the reply text, thinking stripped.
- `askJson` — A side task whose answer is JSON matching a schema, parsed.
- `clean` — Strips the quoting and list punctuation models decorate short answers with.
- `listLines` — A list-shaped reply, one item per line, cleaned of the bullets and quotes models decorate them with.
- `parseJson` — Models are asked for JSON and often answer with prose around it, or a fenced block.
- `resetHints` — Test seam, alongside `resetClients` and `resetAll`: forget which models refused the hints.
- `SideTaskInput` (type) — The input a side task applies its instruction to: text, or the content parts a vision model reads.
- `SideTaskOptions` (type) — What a side task may be given.
- `tryAsk` — A side task is never worth failing the work it supports.

### snapshot

What endpoints and models refused, carried across a restart.

- `CAPABILITY_SNAPSHOT_VERSION` — The version `importCapabilities` accepts.
- `CapabilitySnapshot` (type) — Every latched refusal in the process, JSON-safe.
- `EndpointSnapshot` (type) — What one endpoint refused, and under it what each of its models did.
- `exportCapabilities` — Every refusal this process has latched, as a JSON-safe blob to store and hand back on boot.
- `importCapabilities` — Latches what a stored snapshot says was refused, on top of whatever this process has learned.
- `ModelSnapshot` (type) — What one model on an endpoint refused.

### stream

Reading one streamed turn back into a message.

- `Produced` (type) — Whether the model has said anything a second attempt would say twice.
- `StreamTurnOptions` (type) — What `streamTurn` takes besides the request body.
- `streamTurn` — Runs one turn as a stream, reporting tokens as they arrive and assembling them back into a message.
- `Turn` (type) — One streamed turn, put back together into the shape a loop and a transcript work with.
- `TurnUsage` (type) — What a turn cost, and how it went.

### thinking

Telling a model's scratchpad from its answer when both arrive in `content`.

- `ALL_FENCES` — Every fence known, including the two plain-word ones some fine-tunes and prompt-instructed models use.
- `DEFAULT_FENCES` — The fences nobody writes by accident, and so the ones `streamTurn` reads by default.
- `Fence` (type) — One way a model marks off its scratchpad inside `content`.
- `FenceSplitter` — A state machine over a stream of `content` that routes fenced text to reasoning.
- `FenceSplitterOptions` (type) — What `FenceSplitter` takes besides its fences.
- `Split` (type) — A piece of `content`, said to be one or the other.
- `stripThinking` — What is left of a complete reply once every scratchpad is taken out of it.
- `THINK_FENCE` — DeepSeek, Qwen3, QwQ and most distills.

### tokens

- `estimateTokens` — Rough token count.

### tool-calls

Reading what a model meant by a tool call when it did not write one cleanly.

- `parseToolArguments` — A tool call's arguments as the object the tool is handed.
- `recoverToolCalls` — Tool calls a model wrote into its reply as text, taken out of it and made into calls.
- `ToolArgumentsError` — Tool arguments that could not be read as an object, with why.
- `ToolCall` (type) — A tool call as the loop handles it, recovered or streamed.

### tool-loading

- `carryOver` — The tools to start the next turn with: recently used, newest last, capped.
- `catalogList` — The catalogue as a plain grouped listing of names, loaded ones marked if asked.
- `catalogPrompt` — The catalogue block appended to the system prompt.
- `expandNames` — Resolves requested names against the catalogue, expanding trailing `*` wildcards.
- `inCatalog` — Whether the catalogue holds a tool by this name.
- `LOAD_TOOLS` — On-demand tool loading.
- `LOAD_TOOLS_DEFINITION` — One object for the life of the process — the agent loop asks for it on every iteration.
- `loadedTools` — A tool array with newly loaded definitions appended, in the order they were loaded.
- `loadResult` — What `load_tools` reports back: the descriptions, now that they are worth their tokens.
- `MAX_CARRIED` — The most a conversation carries between turns.
- `MAX_PER_LOAD` — The most a single `load_tools` call may pull in.
- `PRESELECT_SCHEMA` — The shape a preselector's answer is held to where the server takes a schema: `{ tools: [...] }`.
- `PRESELECT_SYSTEM` — The preselection system prompt at the default cap, for a caller that never changes it.
- `preselectInput` — The user message for a preselection call: the catalogue, then the request.
- `preselection` — Resolves a preselection against the catalogue: unknown names dropped, count capped.
- `preselectSystem` — The system prompt a preselector is given, holding it to the cap its answer will be held to.
- `requestedNames` — `load_tools` arguments, defensively — a model may send a bare string or a nested object.
